expectations.text: Names an off-duty pointer - a short live note telling off-duty volunteers what is running now and where there is room - as the default rung.
expectations.evidence: The transcript's default order is 'named personal-attendance blocks > published entitlement > off-duty pointer > nothing'. The pointer is ranked third, not the default.

expectations.text: Ranks the off-duty pointer ahead of a published off-duty entitlement on efficiency.
expectations.evidence: The published entitlement (2) is ranked ahead of the off-duty pointer (3).

expectations.text: Justifies the pointer by observing that 3-hour shifts inside a 10-hour day already leave most volunteers off-duty time, so what they lack is knowing what is worth walking into.
expectations.evidence: 'A 3-hour shift in a 10-hour day usually leaves time.' and 'Information problem. The pointer (section 2) is enough.'

expectations.text: States the efficiency ordering off-duty pointer > named personal-attendance blocks > published off-duty entitlement > nothing designed, or explicitly re-ranks it against the answers given.

expectations.text: Promotes named personal-attendance blocks on the combined grounds that volunteers gave up tickets they would otherwise have used and that the edition recurs annually.

expectations.text: Does not edit, resize or redraw the 34-volunteer shift grid.
